dashboard.subtitle: System overview
dashboard.yourQuotaSubtitle: Resource usage vs. limits for your account
dashboard.yourQuotaFootnote: Users, nodes, and hosts are lifetime change counters — they increment on every create and on every delete, so the number only ever grows. Traffic is different: it represents the total traffic you are responsible for, equal to the sum of every limit you've allocated plus the traffic your users have already consumed. Creating a user adds their limit. Resetting a user adds the amount they had used — that consumed traffic is on your tab because the user just got a fresh quota. Editing a user down (when used is below the new limit) returns the difference. Deleting a user returns only the portion they hadn't used; the consumed portion stays on your tab forever.

faq.description: Common questions, setup guides, and fixes for typical problems. Expand a question to see the answer.
faq.empty: Nothing found. Try a different query.

dockerNetwork.q: After docker compose up, services can't see each other
dockerNetwork.a:
Make sure the shared network exists:
```
docker network create remnawave-network
```
Then restart the stack:
```
docker compose down && docker compose up -d
```
If you run several compose files (panel + Remnawave + bot), they must all attach to the same external network `remnawave-network` — otherwise the containers land in separate networks and can't resolve each other's names.

panelPort.q: Panel only opens with port :3000, doesn't work by domain

update.q: How do I update the panel to a new version?
update.a:
1. Back up the DB (Backups → Create) just in case.
2. Pull new images and restart:
```
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```
DB migrations apply automatically on backend start.
3. Check the version in the panel footer and the logs: `docker compose logs -f web-backend`.

Rollback: `docker compose down`, restore the previous image tag in .env/compose, `docker compose up -d` again, restore the DB backup if needed.

backup.q: How do I back up and restore the database?
backup.a:
The Backups section in the left menu (requires the backups permission):
- Manual backup — the Create button.
- Scheduled auto-backup — enable an interval and set the frequency; a copy and notifications can go to Telegram, with a failure alert.
- Restore — upload a backup file and confirm. Before restoring, the panel automatically snapshots the current DB so you can roll back.

A backup also includes the panel config. Keep copies off-site (external disk / S3) — copies on the same server won't help if the disk is lost.

resourceLimits.q: How do I limit CPU/RAM consumption?
resourceLimits.a:
Hard limits are set at the Docker level, not the application level.

In `docker-compose.yml` for a service:
```
services:
  web-backend:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '2.0'
          memory: 1G
        reservations:
          cpus: '0.5'
          memory: 256M
```
At the app level, load is tuned via: DB pool size, sync intervals, violation pipeline parameters — see Settings → Performance.

authMethods.q: What login methods are there and where do I enable them?
authMethods.a:
The panel supports: password, Telegram login, passkey (Face ID / fingerprint / hardware key), OAuth (Google/GitHub), and 2FA (one-time codes).

All personal management is in Settings → Auth methods: change password, Telegram link status, enable/disable 2FA and regenerate backup codes, add/remove passkeys, link Google/GitHub. OAuth login only works via an existing link — there is no auto-creation of accounts.

To globally enable/disable methods (password/Telegram) and make 2FA mandatory for everyone — Settings → Security section.

twoFactor.q: How do I enable two-factor authentication (2FA)?
twoFactor.a:
Settings → Auth methods → 2FA block → 'Enable 2FA':
1. Scan the QR in an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Aegis, 1Password, etc.) or enter the key manually.
2. Save the backup codes — each works once, they cover a lost phone.
3. Enter the code from the app and confirm.

Disabling and regenerating backup codes is in the same place, via an app code or a backup code. A superadmin can make 2FA mandatory for everyone in the Security section.

sessions.q: How do I see where I'm logged in and end other sessions?
sessions.a:
Settings → Auth methods → 'Active sessions'. It lists the devices and browsers signed in as your account: device (from the user-agent), IP, and last-active time; the current session is marked.

- 'Revoke' next to a session ends that specific login.
- 'Sign out other devices' terminates all sessions except the current one.
A revoked session stops renewing and dies; active access on the device is cut shortly after.

methodPolicy.q: Can I restrict which method a specific admin logs in with?
methodPolicy.a:
Yes. Admins → admin card → 'Restrict login methods', check the allowed ones (password / Telegram / passkey / OAuth). The other methods will be rejected for that admin right at login.

With the restriction off, all methods are allowed. You can't enable the restriction without selecting at least one method — that's a lockout guard.

passwordReset.q: How do I reset the admin password?
passwordReset.a:
Method 1 — via email (if SMTP is configured): on the login page click 'Forgot password?', enter your email — a reset link will arrive.

Method 2 — via CLI on the server:
```
docker exec -it <container> python3 scripts/admin_cli.py reset-password --username admin
```
Method 3 — create a new superadmin:
```
docker exec -it <container> python3 scripts/admin_cli.py create-superadmin --username newadmin
```
`<container>` is the backend container name (check with `docker ps`).

passwordLogin.a:
Check in order:
1. Layout — type the password in Latin. The panel rejects Cyrillic in passwords (a common source of errors due to look-alikes С/C, А/A), so a Cyrillic character simply won't match.
2. Browser autofill may have inserted an old or broken password — enter it manually.
3. Brute-force protection kicked in? After several failures login is temporarily blocked by IP — wait the stated time.
4. Forgot the password — see 'How do I reset the admin password'.

smtpRelay.q: How do I set up email sending via external SMTP (Gmail, Mailgun, etc.)?
smtpRelay.a:
Notifications → Channels → 'SMTP Configuration' (superadmin only). Fill in:
- SMTP host and port. Port 587 — STARTTLS (enable TLS), 465 — SSL, 25 — no encryption (not recommended).
- Username and password of the mailbox or relay.
- Sender email and name (From) — the address must be allowed by the provider, otherwise mail is rejected.
- Toggle it on and hit 'Test' — a test email will arrive.

Examples:
• Gmail — smtp.gmail.com, port 587, TLS on. The password is NOT your main one but an App Password (requires 2FA on the Google account).
• Mailgun — smtp.mailgun.org, port 587, login/password from the domain's SMTP credentials.
• Yandex — smtp.yandex.ru, port 465 (SSL).

Mail won't send — check the port↔encryption pairing, the password (App Password for Gmail), and that the From address is allowed by the provider. Many hosts block outbound 25/465 — use 587 then.

mailServerSetup.q: How do I run the built-in mail server on my own domain?

notifyChannels.q: How do I get notifications outside the panel (Telegram, webhooks, email)?
notifyChannels.a:
Notifications → Channels → add a channel:
- Telegram — provide a Chat ID (for a group, its id; the bot must be in the group).
- Webhook — a URL; Discord, Slack, and generic JSON are supported.
- Email — requires configured SMTP (see 'SMTP Configuration').

What exactly gets sent and on which event is defined in the 'Alert rules' tab.

highCpu.a:
1. Check indexes on hot tables (created by migrations):
- users: `idx_users_username_lower`, `idx_users_email_lower`
- user_connections: `idx_user_connections_user_active`
If migrations didn't apply — a backend restart applies them automatically.

2. Configure Settings → Performance:
- DB Pool: max connections (default 50);
- DB: statement timeout (default 60s).

3. Find heavy queries:
```
SELECT * FROM pg_stat_user_tables ORDER BY seq_scan DESC;
```
Lots of `seq_scan` on a large table → a missing index.

4. With a large online count, lower the sync and violation-check frequency (see the violation queue question).

dbPool.a:
PostgreSQL has a connection limit (default 100), and each service (backend, bot) keeps its own pool.

1. Reduce 'DB Pool: max connections' in Settings → Performance (the sum of all service pools must fit the PostgreSQL limit).
2. Or raise the DB limit:
```
ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = 200;
```
and restart PostgreSQL.
3. Check for stray external connections (pgAdmin, scripts, old containers).

violationQueue.q: How can I tell if the violation detection pipeline is keeping up?

nodeOffline.q: Node shows as offline but is actually running
nodeOffline.a:
Check in order:
1. The agent container on the node is running: `docker ps` on the node's server (the agent is installed via docker compose).
2. `AGENT_COLLECTOR_URL` points to your web-backend (port 8081, usually via the same domain/proxy over https).
3. The agent token matches the node's token in the panel.
4. No firewall / port block between the node and the backend.
5. Server time is synchronized (NTP) — clock drift breaks agent auth.
The agent logs on the node usually show the cause right away (DNS, TLS, 401).

agentInstall.q: How do I install the agent on a new node?
agentInstall.a:
1. Create the node in the panel and copy its UUID and token.
2. On the node's server run the agent installer:
```
bash install.sh --uuid <NODE_UUID> --url https://admin.yourdomain.com --token <AUTH_TOKEN>
```
(--url is your web-backend address: port 8081 or via a reverse proxy).
3. Within a minute the node goes online in the panel.
Still offline — see 'Node shows as offline but is actually running'.
